about: The dungeon quality bar as DATA (docs/world-standards/dungeons.md 'Quality recipe'; numbers from projects/proving/authoring/reports/dungeon-quality-recipe.md section 3.4, owner ruling 2026-10-05, palette per the owner's texture correction: ONE ATLAS, one stone colouring, one wood grain/tone, one metal tone). quality.mjs reads only this file for numbers; a dungeon that must differ records a justified exception in its own authoring/quality-exceptions.json, never an edit here.

references.about: the owner-approved bar: their shipped-light sheets go beside every dungeon's sheet (compare gate)

spaces.about: plan.json space kinds. 'room' spaces carry the per-room recipe; 'passage' spaces (a burrow counts as half a room) only the passage rules. natural = rough rock substrate (noise, no box lumps); everything else is built work.

noise.about: natural roles carry geometry noise (tools/mesh-dc/noise.mjs table in authoring/noise.json, embedded in the exported stamp)
noise.smallUseNote: a dungeon with no natural spaces whose natural-role solids (a hearth back, a rubble fall) are under minNaturalShare of all triangles is not judged; a group is judged for flat ceilings only with >= minDownAreaM2 of downward natural faces

atlas.about: one page (one palette, one texture folder) per dungeon; families share one colouring. Hue is only judged on tiles with enough saturation to have one.
atlas.unfamilied: coatings and special surfaces (lichen, ice, snow, wallpaper, night-glass, water) are not hue-checked, only tint-checked
atlas.calibration: 2026-10-05 on the owner-approved Fieldfast Hall: its warm wood/panelling tints are chroma 0.11-0.12 and its red small-brick / grey smooth-stone sit 0.13-0.15 off the stone saturation mean, so tintChroma 0.12 and satBand 0.16 pass it; the Barrow's reused-and-tinted tiles (dressed-trim 0.16, lichen, small-brick) still fail.
atlas.tintNote: a tint is a multiplier: it may darken (value >= tintMinValue) but its chroma (max-min)/max must stay <= tintChroma, so a tint never makes a new colour

recipe.about: per room (section 3.4). Counts come from reports/source-audit.json (built detail, by object name <space>.<kind>.n), the dressing plan reports (props, bones, fixtures) and the shipped scene (decals, lights).

room.decalsMinNote: 2026-10-13 owner ruling: decals are optional (was 6). A dungeon that has decals makes its own set from its concept frames; the decals gate holds them to it.

passage.about: runs and burrows: bones capped; one light per segment longer than lightEveryM unless it is declared unlit in the plan (an arrival passage)

dungeon.fillNote: 2026-10-06: raised from 1.5. The 1.5 cap ("the Barrow 1.15 is the reference") produced the lights-on-black the owner rejected; the floor is now the readability gate on the rendered views and the fill comes from lighting.json (hemisphere 5, calibrated on rime-hall-light). The approved Fieldfast Hall runs ambient 3.2.

recipe.masonryNote: a built room is MASONRY (detailMinMasonry) when its wallRole is one of masonryRoles or unset (a DC dungeon's default wall is stone); plastered, panelled or papered rooms take detailMin
recipe.ruling: Coordinator ruling 2026-10-05 (owner delegated: "you need to ultimately decide"): per-room floors are set near the MEDIAN room of the owner-approved references (Barrow detail 17 / props 3; Hall detail 23 / props 6), raised where the owner explicitly asked for more (props, decals, visible light sources). Decals stay required although neither reference has any (owner: "you also need decals and more props"). Tombs/ossuaries may exceed bonesMax through a reasoned authoring/quality-exceptions.json entry (dungeons.md: more bones in a tomb).

decals.about: Owner ruling 2026-10-13: decals are optional; a dungeon that has them makes its OWN set from its concept frames (tools/image-request.mjs gen, ids prefixed with the project: <project>-decal-*), and no decal image is reused across dungeons. Fails: a decal texture that is the same file, a byte copy or a perceptual near copy (64-bit difference hash, Hamming distance <= phashMaxDistance) of a decal another dungeon uses; one texture making up more than maxShareOfOne of a dungeon's decals (judged from minForShare decals).

originality.about: no set-piece builder or build script shared with another dungeon. Builders are the Python files of authoring/ (outside lib/, the shared primitive library) and crafted*/setpieces* recipe files. A function shared with another dungeon fails unless it is a shared primitive named here; a whole file mostly copied (line Jaccard) fails.
originality.primitivesNote: hexa..wbox are the Barrow's masonry decomposition helpers (pwall/run/room, recipe 3.7: shared and allowed); _profile.._samples are burrow path sweeping. loculi_holes, timber_arch, hull, crafted, cave and rough lumps are set pieces and are NOT primitives.
originality.referencesAreOriginals: a function shared with a reference dungeon (references above) fails only the other dungeon: the copy, not the original

ignoreProjects.gnawspur-rough: role-noise proof copy of gnawspur-deeps (project.json title says so); not a dungeon of its own

readability.about: the readability floor (owner, zone-3 review 2026-10-06: 'pools of light on black look wrong'; dungeons.md 'near black is a fault'). Measured on the shipped-light views (reports/views/*.png): luma = Rec.709 weights on the sRGB bytes, every sampleStep-th pixel. A view is BLACK when more than view.darkShareMax of it is under nearBlack. The dungeon is judged on its MEDIAN view: near-black share (lights on black), mean luminance band (too dark / too bright) and the 10th percentile (flat: even the darkest tenth is lit, no pools of light).

standard.about: THE interior readability table, one source for every interior target (2026-10-09 dungeon consistency pass; reconciles the light schema's old 'an interior shot averages 70-100', which no shipped dungeon ever met, with this gate's 14-40). Cited by the light component's `intensity` description (packages/core) and tools/dungeon-pipeline/lighting.json. Two scales of the same light: PROBE = what a mid-grey matte sphere and two reference characters read at chest height in a room's lit floor area, camera 4 m (apps/playground/tools/light-shots.mts --spots); VIEW = what a whole player-height picture reads (the gate below, on reports/views). Luma = Rec.709 on 0-255 sRGB. Mood is tone (the fill's hue, the fixtures' colour), never brightness.

probe.poolNote: above 80 only inside a fixture's pool; the dungeons' per-dungeon median probe within acrossDungeonsMax of each other in comparable rooms

standard.view: readability.dungeon below (the gate on reports/views): median view mean in [meanMin, meanMax], darkest tenth <= p10Max (pools, not a flat wash), near-black share <= darkShareMedianMax (not lights on black)

readability.calibration: 2026-10-06 on the shipped views as they stood. fieldfast-hall (owner-approved bar): median near-black 0.48, mean 21, p10 3, worst view 0.86 -> passes. gnawspur-deeps (owner: 'very bright'): median near-black 0.10, mean 32, p10 14 -> FAILS flat. rime-hall (owner: 'lights on black, horrendous'): median near-black 0.80, mean 9, three views >= 0.95 -> FAILS. fieldfast-barrow's checked-in views: median near-black 0.93, mean 6.6 -> FAILS (the views predate the barrow's current light or the owner judged it in play; re-shoot before acting). RECALIBRATED 2026-10-09 (dungeon consistency pass, readability.standard): all four now run the shared lighting stage (hemisphere fill 4.5, Gnawspur 4.0; one post preset). The probe standard (grey sphere 60-80) is ~35% brighter than the old fieldfast-hall flat fill (sphere 54), so meanMax 40 -> 45; meanMin, p10Max and the near-black limits stay. Measured on fresh views: fieldfast-hall mean 27.4 / near-black 0.36 / p10 4; fieldfast-barrow 40.8 / 0.14 / 9; rime-hall 32.0 / 0.23 / 8; gnawspur-deeps 41.5 / 0.05 / 17 -> FAILS flat (its 26 scene torches at intensity 10, range 12-18 m blanket every floor; a fixture fix, not a fill fix).

levels.about: A dungeon's LIGHT LEVEL (owner, 2026-10-09: 'I did like barrows darker; I'm ok with dungeons mimicking night lighting, it all depends'). A dungeon picks one in its authoring/lighting.json (`level`, default lit); lighting.json `levels` sets the fill each level gets, and the gate judges the median view against that level's band. `lit` is the interior standard above (readability.dungeon, readability.standard.probe). `night` is outdoor-night dark (proving at 22:00 reads a grey probe ~35): moody and dim, still never pitch black, so a character can be read and a room's shape seen.

night.calibration: 2026-10-09: set beside outdoor night (proving 22:00 after the consistency pass: grey 32-42, light gear 38-41, dark 11-23). The barrow before the dungeon pass (sphere 5, views mean 6.6, near-black 0.93) is darker than this and fails it: night is dark, not black.

matte.about: matte unless intended (owner, zone-3 review 2026-10-06: 'materials gained a SHEEN'). Judged: every painted atlas role (the dc-palette layer's roughness), the palette's own base, every other material asset of the project (schema defaults when left out: roughness 1, metalness 0 since 2026-10-06; 0.85 / 0.05 before) and the project's own GLB materials (glTF: a factor left out is 1). A role or material whose name carries a metalRoles word may be metal and a little smoother. An intended shine (ice, water, polished black ice) is a quality exception with a why.
matte.sources: 2026-10-06 sheen sources found: per-project materials.mjs layer roughness (rime-hall smooth-stone 0.3, ice 0.35, metal 0.5, silt 0.6; gnawspur-deeps metal 0.45, smooth-stone 0.7; fieldfast-barrow smooth-stone 0.55, metal 0.45), rime-hall frozen-dead 0.5 / ice-skin 0.12 on the statues, the material schema default 0.85 / 0.05 (64 voxel-demo materials leave it out) and Blender-default 0.5 roughness on a few town GLBs.

culling.about: interior pop-in (owner, zone-3 review 2026-10-06: 'walk halfway through a great hall then everything pops into place'). For every interior culling unit in a ROOM (its dressing group), walk the plan route: where the walker first enters the room, the unit must already be revealed (pop-in <= popinMaxM metres walked inside). The scene's cullingProfile (docs/culling.md 'Interior scenes') is applied as the renderer applies it. Bounds are the members' origins padded by propPadM.

compare.about: a sheet of this dungeon's shipped-light views beside the references, newer than the views

stairs.about: stair/ramp headroom (owner 2026-10-06: a stair ceiling follows the stair, a raked slab or a raking vault, never a flat slab the flight runs up into or a stepped roof). Along every stair/ramp line (plan run profiles with steps, burrow floorProfiles that change height, room-kit stair markers), from 1 m before the first riser to 1 m past the last, every sampleM metres on the centre line and at +-(width/2 - bodyEdgeM): cast down to the walking surface, then up to the first downward face. Clear = ceiling - walking surface. minClearM is the human floor; the band (max - min clear on one line) must stay under max(spreadM, spreadRel x median clear) (a flat ceiling over a rise R spreads by ~R); a ceiling that changes by more than maxJumpM within jumpM beyond what the walk's own pitch explains is a stepped roof (a riser-scale step in the roof; DC rounds a vertical step over 1-2 voxels). Drops narrower than ribM (transverse ribs, arch rings) are max-filtered out before the jump test. Natural (rough rock) stairs: the lane edges are judged for minClearM only, the centre line for the band and steps.

arrival.about: dungeon arrival safe zone (real-client portal test 2026-10-06: a ghost 15 m from fieldfast-hall's arrival pinned the player under the fight lock, 'cannot leave in the middle of a fight'). No pack (its spread included), patrol point, named creature, miniboss or boss within safeM of any arrival or exit anchor (plan anchors named entry-* / exit-* / arrival*). Straight-line 3D distance in plan metres: never longer than the walk, so it errs on the safe side.

loot.about: instance loot coverage (owner ruling 2026-10-08): every instance has a reason to go for every class. authoring/loot.json lists the instance's drops; every armor weight drops, every armor slot drops in at least minWeightsPerSlot weights, every weapon role drops, trash has its own table, every named and the boss drop something, rarity stays within the level band, ornament parts only on rare+, and every listed drop is wired (item file exists, the source's loot string names it).
